newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil central banker Lopes confirms he to stay.
newsitem.headline: Brazil central banker Lopes confirms he to stay.

text.p: The Director of Monetary Policy at Brazil's Central Bank, Francisco "Chico" Lopes, said Thursday he would not be leaving the bank's boardroom following the resignation of its head, Gustavo Loyola.
Lopes also confirmed that the bank's Director of Banking Supervision, Claudio Mauch, would remain.
He said both had been invited by Gustavo Franco, the bank's Director of International Affairs who has been nominated to take over the presidency from Loyola, to stay on and both had accepted.

"There will be no changes in foreign exchange policy," Lopes said, adding he considered Brazil's current economic policies "consistent" and denying he and Franco had ever disagreed over monetary policy.

The Central Bank said Wednesday that Director of Controls Alkimar Moura would follow Loyola's lead and resign. Moura's exit had been agreed a long time ago, the bank said, and was not directly related to the changes at the helm.
On Wednesday, rumors began to circulate in Brasilia and in the markets that Lopes too might resign. Lopes has long been identified as more flexible a monetarist than Franco.
Replacements for Franco and Moura are expected to be announced Friday.
